subject: Creative Arts

accessibility: Read prompts and choices aloud when needed. Practical responses may use classroom materials, movement, speech or drawing.

indicators.statement: Explore own experiences to talk about visual artworks that reflect the history and culture of people in other Ghanaian communities.

skills.description: Identify the subject, artistic method and evidence in a work.

questions.stem: A class studies a strip of cloth from another Ghanaian community. The weaver shows how threads cross. What is this work about?
options: A tree beside a school gate
A bridge over a river
A weaver at work
Saving water at school
questions.answer: A weaver at work
hints: Identify the action or subject at the centre.
questions.explanation: The described action centres on a weaver at work.

questions.stem: A class studies a strip of cloth from another Ghanaian community. The weaver shows how threads cross. Which detail could a learner point out in the work?
options: A wrapper just above an open bin
A straight band above a winding blue line
A hand on the tap above three drops
Light threads crossing dark threads
questions.answer: Light threads crossing dark threads
hints: Look for a detail the example actually describes.
questions.explanation: The evidence in the example is light threads crossing dark threads.

questions.stem: A class studies a strip of cloth from another Ghanaian community. The weaver shows how threads cross. Which method is used?
options: Printing blue drops beside a drawn tap
Drawing lines of different shapes
Rubbing a leaf and drawing the gate
Weaving strips over and under
questions.answer: Weaving strips over and under
hints: Think about how the parts were made or performed.
questions.explanation: The example uses weaving strips over and under to show a weaver at work.

questions.stem: Which source could help us learn the history of another Ghanaian community?

A rumour with no known source
A made-up date on a new drawing

hints: Look for evidence of what happened in that community.
questions.explanation: Look for evidence of what happened in that community. A reliable story from a knowledgeable community member.

questions.stem: A pot has a wide mouth and two handles. What might its handles help a person do?

Close its mouth

Add a louder shaker to cover the quiet words.
Keep the group singing and soften the shaker under the words.
Ask the audience to guess the missing words.

questions.stem: A class imagines a landing in another Ghanaian town. Performers sway like boats and then mime pulling a rope. Which reading of the work is supported by the example?

Everyone can help keep a shared space tidy

questions.stem: A class imagines a landing in another Ghanaian town. Performers sway like boats and then mime pulling a rope. Which source could help the reviewer check a claim about the subject?

questions.stem: A class imagines a landing in another Ghanaian town. Performers sway like boats and then mime pulling a rope. Which suggestion gives the maker a specific next step?

Face the bucket towards the audience as it passes

Hold the pulling shape at the end

Keep swaying freely without changing the movement.
End with all hands waving above the head.
Let the dancers scatter before they reach the landing.

questions.stem: A class imagines a landing in another Ghanaian town. Performers sway like boats and then mime pulling a rope. A partner wants to know why the artist chose this method. Which reply explains the choice?
